{{Short description|Theory in physics}}
{{no footnotes|date=January 2014}}

{{general relativity}}

In [[physics]], '''relativistic chaos''' is the application of [[chaos theory]] to [[dynamical system]]s described primarily by [[general relativity]], and also [[special relativity]].

[[John D. Barrow]] showed in 1982 that the [[Einstein field equations]] exhibit chaotic behaviour and modelled the [[Mixmaster universe]] as a dynamical system.<ref>{{cite journal
 |author=J. D. Barrow
 |year=1982
 |title=General relativistic chaos and nonlinear dynamics
 |journal=[[General Relativity and Gravitation]]
 |volume=14 |issue=6 |pages=523–530
 |bibcode=1982GReGr..14..523B
 |doi=10.1007/BF00756214
 |s2cid=121254445
 |url=http://plouffe.fr/simon/math/math10280.pdf
}}</ref> Later work showed that relativistic chaos is coordinate invariant.<ref>{{cite journal
 |author=A. E. Motter
 |year=2003
 |title=Relativistic chaos is coordinate invariant
 |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]
 |volume=93 |issue=23 |article-number=231101
 |arxiv=gr-qc/0305020
 |bibcode=2003PhRvL..91w1101M
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.91.231101
 |pmid=14683170
 |s2cid=32645063
 |url=http://chaosbook.org/library/Motter03.pdf
}}</ref>
